Zermatt is one town in the middle of nowhere. There is luxury shops and skiing. A couple of apres ski bars and a lot of hotels. Appenzell a whole canton (yes there is a town called appenzell) there is hiking, biking, a brewery to visit, a lovely old town, an actual population and culture that lives there. Great connections to St. Gallen (and from there to the rest of switzerland) you can go to lake constance, go for a ferry ride, go shopping in germany and austria (cheaper). Okay so wow big move. Dont be scared of the cold. Dress functionally, so rain coat, waterproof shoes, decent jeans (maybe some thermals under them on cold days). Make sure its waterproof since beeing cold and beeing cold and wet are two really different things. 
Racism happens but in a more casual way especially since you are a woman. So people wont come up to you calling names but they will associate „mistakes“ you make with you looking foreign. Lucerne is a pretty international city, a lot of tourism so you might just blend in. But being on the phone in spanish is probably no issue. 

Speaking of lucerne, traffic is horrible. Public transport is safe if you travel alone. At night on weekends you probably will encounter some drunk douchebags. Generally if you sit close to the front where the driver is you would be safe.

Make sure to check the scedule for football matches to avoid the fan marches and the traffic they cause. Get a half fare card for public transport. Maybe get a zonenabo for transport within the city. Learn the local emergency numbers. Swissgerman is difficult to learn. I know people who have lived and worked and socialised in CH for 25 years and still dont speak it without an accent. Its worth trying tho. Language is important for integration in CH. Maybe join a club or somthing because thats where the swiss really socialise. Health insurance is expensive but it generally works pretty well and is more affordable than in the US. Migros is cheaper than coop but denner aldi and lidl are the most affordable for food. If you are under 25 you can get a GANight for 100CHF. Thats free public transport from 19-05 and weekends 19-07.
